paragraphs: Learning a symbolic model means turning experience with an environment into an abstract description that an agent can use. This paper asks how an agent should collect experience so that this model becomes useful with less data. Its approach makes exploration depend on what the current model still does not know.

The algorithm has two cooperating parts. One quickly constructs an intermediate Bayesian symbolic model from observations collected so far. The other uses that model to guide exploration toward uncertain regions of the state space. Because the process operates online, newly collected experience can inform subsequent exploration rather than serving only as input to a final model.

The authors report better performance than random and greedy exploration in two computer game domains. An Asteroids-inspired game emphasizes complex dynamics with simple logical structure, while the Treasure Game emphasizes more complex logic with simpler dynamics. These contrasting settings support the usefulness of uncertainty-guided exploration for learning symbolic representations across different kinds of environmental complexity.
neurips-2017-active-exploration-for-lear.tldr: An online agent learns symbolic environment models more efficiently by directing exploration toward its model’s uncertainties.

paragraphs: The paper studies linear models that predict several responses at once while using many parameters with an underlying structure. Its central observation is that noise across the responses can be correlated. Those relationships provide information that an estimation procedure can exploit when learning the model parameters.

The proposed alternating estimation procedure, AltEst, builds on the generalized Dantzig selector. The theoretical question is how the estimation error changes as the procedure progresses. Under suitable sample-size and resampling assumptions, the authors show that the error decreases at a linear rate with high probability until it reaches a particular achievable floor. Linear convergence here describes repeated proportional reduction toward that floor, rather than an assurance that error disappears.

The error floor is expressed through geometric quantities associated with the parameter structure, including Gaussian width. This connects statistical accuracy to the shape of the structured estimation problem. The authors identify their result as the first finite-sample statistical guarantee for an alternating procedure of this kind accommodating general structures.
neurips-2017-alternating-estimation-for-.tldr: AltEst exploits correlated response noise and, under stated sampling assumptions, converges geometrically toward a structure-dependent estimation error floor.

paragraphs: Asynchronous block coordinate descent lets parallel workers update parts of an optimization problem without waiting for one another. That can avoid costly synchronization, but workers may act on outdated shared variables. The paper examines convergence theory whose assumptions about those outdated values and update choices can conflict with practical implementations.

In particular, earlier analyses assume that the age of a worker’s information is independent of the block it updates, and that blocks are selected randomly. The authors remove the independence requirement throughout their analysis. They also accommodate both random selection and essentially cyclic deterministic selection, bringing the theory closer to a broader range of update schedules.

The convergence results cover settings with bounded or unbounded delays and include nonconvex, weakly convex, and strongly convex objectives under the analyzed assumptions. A Lyapunov function tracks both progress on the objective and the effects of delays. A continuous-time differential equation motivates this construction, helping explain how stale information can be incorporated directly into a convergence argument.
neurips-2017-asynchronous-coordinate-des.tldr: The paper proves asynchronous coordinate descent convergence under broader update schedules and delay assumptions that better reflect practical implementations.

paragraphs: The paper studies how to balance exposure to two opposing viewpoints spreading through a social network. It assumes that people have different preferences toward the two campaigns. A centralized decision-maker chooses a set of participants for each campaign, seeking balanced information exposure across the network rather than optimizing either campaign in isolation.

The authors formulate balance using a symmetric difference function, which captures disagreement between the campaigns’ exposure sets. This objective lacks two properties often useful in influence optimization: monotonicity and submodularity. Consequently, adding participants does not provide the familiar structural guarantees that would make existing approaches directly applicable.

The contribution includes a formal problem definition, a characterization of computational hardness, approximation algorithms, and experimental evaluation. Its guarantees concern a global objective controlled by one decision-maker. This differs from analyzing the final move of competing, self-interested agents. The work therefore makes balanced exposure a distinct optimization target, with algorithmic challenges arising from the relationship between the two campaigns.
neurips-2017-balancing-information-expos.tldr: The paper develops approximation algorithms for centrally selecting campaign participants to balance exposure to two opposing viewpoints in a social network.

paragraphs: Value-based reinforcement learning estimates how worthwhile actions are, while policy-based learning represents how actions should be chosen. This paper connects the two through entropy regularization and a softmax form of temporal consistency. It shows that action values satisfying this consistency relationship correspond to optimal entropy-regularized policy probabilities along any action sequence, regardless of how that sequence was obtained.

The authors turn this relationship into Path Consistency Learning, or PCL. The algorithm minimizes a soft consistency error across sequences of multiple actions. It can use both on-policy traces, generated by the current policy, and off-policy traces. This makes the theoretical connection directly useful as a training objective over different sources of experience.

The paper interprets PCL as generalizing actor-critic and Q-learning approaches. It also shows how one model can represent both a policy and its associated softmax state values, removing the need for a separate critic. Across several benchmarks, the reported evaluation finds significant improvements over strong actor-critic and Q-learning baselines.
neurips-2017-bridging-the-gap-between-va.tldr: Path Consistency Learning connects values and policies through entropy-regularized consistency and learns from both on-policy and off-policy action sequences.

paragraphs: Distributed training can concentrate communication at a central node, making that node a bottleneck. This paper asks whether decentralized parallel stochastic gradient descent can outperform a centralized implementation even when both arrangements are available. The question concerns training efficiency, rather than decentralization being the only possible network arrangement.

The theoretical analysis identifies a regime where decentralized training might be faster. Its total computational complexity is comparable to that of centralized training, while its busiest node handles much less communication. This separates the amount of computation from the communication burden concentrated at a particular location, explaining how similar computational requirements can lead to different runtimes.

The authors test this argument using CNTK and Torch, multiple network configurations, and platforms with up to 112 GPUs. On networks with low bandwidth or high latency, decentralized training can be up to an order of magnitude faster than well-optimized centralized counterparts. The result supports a conditional advantage: the communication environment matters substantially to whether decentralization improves speed.
neurips-2017-can-decentralized-algorithm.tldr: Decentralized stochastic gradient descent can outperform centralized training when communication bottlenecks dominate, with reported speedups up to an order of magnitude.

paragraphs: Policy-gradient reinforcement learning commonly involves preliminary warm-start training and procedures for reducing sampling variance. The paper treats these as undesirable overhead and proposes a method that requires neither. Its goal is to retain advantages of policy-gradient learning while making the training procedure simpler to use.

The method is built around a softmax value function. The authors describe it as combining policy-gradient benefits with the efficiency and simplicity of maximum-likelihood approaches. The cold-start property concerns the training setup: the proposed method does not depend on a separate warm-start phase. Likewise, dispensing with a variance-reduction procedure is a claim about what the method requires, rather than a claim that sampling has no variability.

The application is sequence generation for structured output prediction, where a model must produce an entire organized output. The authors provide empirical evidence from automatic summarization and image captioning. These results support the proposed training approach in two sequence-generation tasks and connect its procedural simplification to concrete prediction problems.
neurips-2017-cold-start-reinforcement-le.tldr: A softmax-value reinforcement learning method trains sequence generators without requiring warm-start training or a separate sampling-variance reduction procedure.

paragraphs: Dual Path Networks combine two ways of passing information through an image model. The paper relates ResNet and DenseNet within the HORNN framework, interpreting residual connections as supporting feature reuse and dense connections as supporting exploration of new features. Both capabilities are treated as useful for learning representations.

The proposed architecture provides paths that share common features while preserving flexibility to develop additional ones. This turns the relationship between the existing architectures into a modular network design. The aim is to keep useful representations available while allowing the network to expand what it represents.

Experiments report superior results across ImageNet-1k, Places365, and PASCAL VOC tasks. On ImageNet-1k, a shallow DPN exceeds the named ResNeXt-101 comparator with a 26% smaller model, 25% less computation, and 8% lower memory consumption. A deeper DPN-131 advances reported single-model performance with about twice the training speed. Scene recognition, detection, and segmentation evaluations also show improvements over DenseNet, ResNet, and ResNeXt, supporting the design across several visual applications.
neurips-2017-dual-path-networks-c9b9b9d5.tldr: Dual Path Networks combine feature reuse and new-feature exploration, delivering reported accuracy and efficiency improvements across several visual tasks.

paragraphs: EEG-GRAPH uses relationships across recording locations and time to infer pathological brain activity from electroencephalograms. Its application is identifying brain regions that generate seizures in people with epilepsy. The model jointly considers these dependencies so that evidence about instantaneous activity is interpreted in its spatial and temporal context.

The authors represent the problem with a factor graph and design its factor functions using domain knowledge. These functions express how different pieces of evidence relate within the model. A graph-cut-based inference procedure solves the resulting graph inference exactly in polynomial time. Exactness concerns solving the model’s inference problem; it does not make the biological predictions automatically certain.

Evaluation uses clinically collected intracranial EEG from 29 patients. The reported AUC is 0.72, compared with 0.67 and 0.65 for two conventional localization approaches. The proposed inference method also exceeds sampling-based alternatives with AUCs of 0.62 and 0.69. These results support both the joint modeling approach and the particular inference procedure for the evaluated localization task.
neurips-2017-eeg-graph-a-factor-graph-ba.tldr: EEG-GRAPH combines spatial and temporal EEG evidence with exact graph-cut inference to improve seizure-region localization in the reported patient evaluation.

paragraphs: Latent-variable models often use the evidence lower bound, or ELBO, as a practical substitute for directly maximizing likelihood. This paper develops a family of alternative lower bounds called filtering variational objectives, or FIVOs. Their construction uses a particle filter’s estimate of the marginal likelihood.

FIVOs take the same arguments as the ELBO but can use a model’s sequential structure to obtain tighter bounds. A tighter bound provides a closer surrogate for the likelihood being optimized. The authors analyze this connection through the broader class of bounds formed by taking logarithms of likelihood estimators, relating bound tightness to the variance of the particle filter’s estimate.

Experiments on sequential data compare training the same model architecture with FIVO and with the ELBO. The reported substantial improvements therefore demonstrate the importance of the training objective within that comparison, without requiring an architectural change. The contribution links a sequential inference procedure, the quality of its likelihood estimate, and the objective used to fit the model.
neurips-2017-filtering-variational-objec.tldr: Filtering variational objectives use particle-filter likelihood estimates to exploit sequential structure and improve reported training results over the ELBO.

paragraphs: Kernel regression depends on how the model judges similarity between inputs. This paper studies learning that notion of similarity for the Nadaraya-Watson estimator, rather than relying only on standard adjustments such as bandwidth selection. It argues that a learned metric can substantially reduce prediction error, particularly when the data have many dimensions.

The proposed procedure derives an efficient way to learn the metric by analyzing the estimator for Gaussian-distributed data. Its distinguishing feature is that the resulting estimator draws on both global and local structure in the training set. The similarity function can therefore reflect broader patterns while still responding to the structure relevant near a prediction.

The authors provide theoretical and empirical results showing that the learned metric can considerably reduce both bias and mean squared error. These benefits also appear beyond Gaussian data, so the distribution used to develop the method does not confine all of its reported benefits. The findings emphasize that choosing the geometry of similarity can be an important part of improving kernel regression.
neurips-2017-generative-local-metric-lea.tldr: Learning a metric from global and local data structure can reduce kernel-regression bias and mean squared error, including beyond Gaussian data.

paragraphs: Eventually escaping a saddle point does not establish that an optimization method will escape quickly. This paper makes that distinction concrete for gradient descent. Although gradient descent almost always escapes saddles asymptotically, the authors show that saddle points can still delay its progress for an exponentially long time.

The result holds even with fairly natural random initialization schemes and functions described as non-pathological. Thus, the slowdown cannot simply be dismissed as requiring an obviously artificial starting point or a severely irregular objective. The claim establishes a possible computational obstacle for gradient descent, rather than saying that every problem or every saddle causes exponential delay.

The paper contrasts this behavior with perturbed gradient descent, which can reach an approximate local minimizer in polynomial time in the theoretical comparison. This provides a reason to introduce perturbations when efficient nonconvex optimization matters. Experiments illustrate the theoretical findings, while the main contribution is the separation between an eventual-escape guarantee and a useful bound on the time required.
neurips-2017-gradient-descent-can-take-e.tldr: Gradient descent can take exponential time to escape saddles, establishing a theoretical efficiency advantage for perturbations in the analyzed comparison.

paragraphs: Continual learning asks a model to acquire new abilities while retaining knowledge from earlier tasks. The paper studies a setting where examples arrive once, one at a time, across a sequence of tasks. This makes the learning process itself central: success depends on what survives and transfers as experience accumulates.

The authors first propose evaluation metrics that go beyond test accuracy. These also characterize knowledge transfer between tasks, allowing evaluation to distinguish successful learning from harmful forgetting and beneficial reuse. That broader perspective matters because two models with similar accuracy can differ in how their experiences affect performance across the task sequence.

The proposed model, Gradient Episodic Memory, alleviates forgetting while permitting beneficial transfer to previous tasks. Later learning can therefore help earlier tasks as well as threaten their retained knowledge. Experiments on variants of MNIST and CIFAR-100 report strong performance relative to the state of the art. The contribution combines a continual-learning method with an evaluation framework that makes cross-task effects explicit.
neurips-2017-gradient-episodic-memory-fo.tldr: Gradient Episodic Memory reduces forgetting while allowing later learning to benefit earlier tasks, alongside metrics for evaluating cross-task transfer.

paragraphs: This paper investigates recurrent highway networks and recurrent hypernetworks as complementary approaches to language modeling. It adds experimental evidence where prior treatment emphasized theory and examines theoretical questions where prior work emphasized experiments. The aim is both to explain these architectures more fully and to test what combining them achieves.

For recurrent highway networks, the authors report substantially better gradient flow than LSTMs alongside improved task accuracy. For hypernetworks, they analyze unresolved theoretical issues and propose feasible solutions that they believe could yield future gains. Those proposed gains remain a forward-looking expectation, distinct from the results demonstrated by the combined model.

Combining the two approaches significantly improves reported state-of-the-art character-level language modeling on Penn Treebank while using much simpler regularization. This supports their compatibility in the evaluated task. The authors also advocate recurrent highway networks as replacements for LSTMs and hypernetworks as a standard augmentation for recurrent architectures. Those broader recommendations extend the interpretation of the evidence beyond the specific benchmark result.
neurips-2017-language-modeling-with-recu.tldr: Combining recurrent highway networks and hypernetworks improves reported Penn Treebank character modeling while using simpler regularization.

paragraphs: Calcium imaging measures neural activity indirectly and noisily, while optical stimulation can introduce additional artifacts. This paper develops a Bayesian model that jointly infers neural spikes and connectivity from experiments combining these techniques. Joint inference lets uncertainty about spikes affect inferred connections, and uncertainty about connections affect inferred spikes.

The model uses a variational-autoencoder framework with discrete latent variables for spiking activity, a low-dimensional representation of shared input, and sparse spike-and-slab coupling between neurons. It also explicitly models stimulation of unintended targets and stimulation-related transients. These components address both the underlying circuit and distortions introduced by the experimental intervention.

The authors report fitting 30 minutes of data in 10 minutes. They apply the method to an all-optical mapping experiment in the primary visual cortex of an awake mouse, predicting connections among excitatory neurons in layer 2/3. The predicted connectivity is sparse and agrees with known relationships involving stimulus tuning, spontaneous correlation, and distance. This agreement supports the plausibility of the inferred connectivity.
neurips-2017-model-based-bayesian-infere.tldr: A joint Bayesian model infers neural spikes and connectivity from optical experiments while accounting for uncertainty and stimulation artifacts.

paragraphs: Predictors can influence an outcome through combinations involving several variables, rather than only through separate effects. This paper proposes a Bayesian regression model that accommodates interactions of arbitrary order. Its scope therefore includes relationships involving more than pairs of predictors, with interaction structure forming part of the modeling problem.

The model uses factorization to represent interaction coefficients and a prior over random hypergraphs to guide which interactions are selected. A hypergraph can represent groups containing multiple predictors, matching the multi-way nature of the relationships being considered. The prior construction generalizes the Finite Feature Model, while posterior inference is carried out with a Gibbs-sampling algorithm.

The authors establish posterior consistency, providing theoretical support for the model’s statistical behavior as evidence accumulates under the result’s conditions. Extensive simulated-data experiments evaluate the method, and applications in genetics and retail demand forecasting demonstrate its ability to identify meaningful interactions. The contribution brings interaction representation, selection, and Bayesian inference into a single regression approach.
neurips-2017-multi-way-interacting-regre.tldr: A Bayesian factorization model uses random-hypergraph priors to select multi-way predictor interactions and identifies meaningful relationships in reported applications.

paragraphs: Visual question answering requires a model to connect a question with entities and relationships in an image. The paper argues that a common design, pairing question processing with a single image representation, restricts this reasoning. One general visual summary may contain only limited information about the image contents relevant to different questions.

The authors introduce a modular neural network that learns a multimodal, multifaceted representation of both image and question. Its purpose is to make several aspects of the visual and linguistic information available for reasoning. The model then learns to use that combined representation when reasoning about the entities in the image.

The reported experiments achieve new state-of-the-art performance by a wide margin on both VQA v1.0 and VQA v2.0. These findings support the proposed representation and reasoning approach on two VQA benchmarks. The broader significance is that how image and language information are represented together can influence the model’s ability to answer questions, beyond simply supplying each modality to a neural network.
neurips-2017-multimodal-learning-and-rea.tldr: A modular network learns multifaceted image-and-question representations and reports substantial improvements on both VQA benchmarks.

paragraphs: Neural networks initially tend to produce similar outputs for nearby inputs. The paper identifies a mismatch between this smooth bias and value functions in reinforcement learning with sparse rewards. When rewards arrive, the relevant value structure can have an asymmetric discontinuity, making a purely smooth approximation harder to learn.

The proposed mechanism learns how to interpolate between two estimates. One is a direct estimate of value. The other projects value using the encountered reward and the previous estimate. Combining them reduces how much discontinuous structure the model must learn directly, using information already available from the transition in experience.

The interpolation depends on the state and is itself learned, allowing the method to adjust how much it trusts the projected estimate. The authors state that this also accommodates heterogeneous observability, where the available information varies across situations. Adding this mechanism to A3C produces significant improvements on multiple Atari games. The results support adapting value estimation to reward-driven discontinuities through a learned use of past estimates.
neurips-2017-natural-value-approximators.tldr: Learning when to combine direct values with reward-adjusted past estimates improves value approximation and reported A3C performance on multiple Atari games.

paragraphs: Extrapolation methods use several recent optimization iterates to construct a better estimate of the optimum. Although this strategy had strong convergence results in deterministic settings, stochastic optimization introduces noise into those iterates. This paper studies whether extrapolation can still improve progress when applied to ordinary or already accelerated stochastic gradient methods.

The analysis first derives convergence bounds allowing arbitrary perturbations, including perturbations that may be biased. It then develops asymptotic bounds in terms of the relationship between noise variance and the accuracy of the current point. This makes the noise level relative to optimization progress an explicit part of the theory, rather than treating stochastic iterates as if they were exact.

The authors apply the acceleration technique to SGD, SAGA, SVRG, and Katyusha in different settings and report significant performance gains. The findings show that extrapolation can complement several stochastic optimization procedures, including an accelerated one. The theoretical and experimental contributions together address how information across recent iterates remains useful despite perturbations.
neurips-2017-nonlinear-acceleration-of-s.tldr: The paper analyzes extrapolation under stochastic perturbations and reports acceleration gains for several stochastic optimization algorithms.

paragraphs: Training a neural network on a new task can erase information useful for an earlier one. Incremental moment matching, or IMM, addresses this catastrophic forgetting by combining information from networks trained on successive tasks. Its central object is the posterior distribution over network parameters, rather than only the performance of the latest network.

IMM incrementally matches moments of the task-specific posterior distributions. Moments summarize properties of a distribution, so matching them provides a way to reconcile information learned from different tasks. The procedure is supported by transfer-learning techniques intended to smooth the search space for posterior parameters: weight transfer, an L2 relationship between old and new parameters, and a dropout variant using old parameters.

The authors evaluate the approach on MNIST, CIFAR-10, Caltech-UCSD-Birds, and Lifelog. They report state-of-the-art experimental performance through balancing information between the old and new networks. The findings support this combination of posterior matching and transfer techniques as a way to retain earlier knowledge while incorporating new learning.
neurips-2017-overcoming-catastrophic-for.tldr: Incremental moment matching combines task-specific parameter posteriors and transfer techniques to balance new learning with retained knowledge.

paragraphs: Many sparse-learning problems can be written as linear programs controlled by a regularization parameter. This paper studies solving a broad class of these problems with the parametric simplex method. A central benefit is obtaining the complete solution path as regularization varies, giving access to more than a solution at one selected setting.

The method also provides a high-precision stopping criterion through a dual certificate. The authors emphasize that it can produce sparse solutions in very few iterations and that sparsity reduces the work required within each iteration. Thus, sparsity matters both as a property sought in the learned model and as a source of computational savings.

The paper considers the Dantzig selector for regression, sparse support vector machines for classification, and sparse differential network estimation. It provides sufficient conditions under which the method always produces sparse solutions, supporting the associated computational benefit under those conditions. Numerical experiments report strong performance across the studied approaches, connecting the theoretical sparsity argument with practical optimization results.
neurips-2017-parametric-simplex-method-f.tldr: The parametric simplex method efficiently traces regularization paths for sparse linear programs, with sparsity guarantees under sufficient conditions.

paragraphs: The paper addresses the difficulty of estimating a probability distribution over several variables without prescribing a rigid form for that distribution. Such nonparametric estimation faces both statistical and computational obstacles. The authors note that more practical approaches often obtain tractability by imposing assumptions that bring their models close to parametric ones, reducing the flexibility that motivates nonparametric modeling.

Their proposal is a class of models built around conditional distributions: the distribution of one variable when the values of the others are given. The central assumption is that each of these conditional distributions belongs to a nonparametric exponential family. This places structure on the functions describing the conditionals while retaining a nonparametric formulation.

The significance is the authors’ claim that this conditional construction yields attractive computational and statistical properties. It offers an approach to flexible multivariate density estimation whose organizing restriction is explicit. The proposed flexibility therefore depends on the stated exponential-family assumption for every variable’s conditional distribution; it does not amount to removing all assumptions about the density.
neurips-2017-the-expxorcist-nonparametri.tldr: The paper proposes nonparametric models with attractive computational and statistical properties by assuming that each variable’s conditional distribution has a nonparametric exponential-family form.

paragraphs: Training deep residual networks requires intermediate activations to calculate gradients during backpropagation. Keeping these activations in memory becomes a bottleneck as networks grow deeper and wider. This paper changes the network architecture so that most of those intermediate values can be recovered when needed.

The proposed Reversible Residual Network, or RevNet, allows a layer’s activations to be reconstructed exactly from those of the next layer. This reversibility removes the need to retain activations for most layers throughout backpropagation. The central idea is to make recoverability a property of the model’s computation, directly addressing the storage demands of gradient calculation.

Experiments on CIFAR and ImageNet show nearly identical performance to ResNets of equal size. At the same time, the reported activation-storage requirement is independent of network depth. That claim specifically concerns activation storage, the bottleneck targeted by the architecture. The findings show that substantial changes to how training retains intermediate information can preserve the predictive performance of the compared residual networks.
neurips-2017-the-reversible-residual-net.tldr: RevNets reconstruct intermediate activations during backpropagation, making activation storage independent of depth while nearly matching equally sized ResNets.

paragraphs: Mondrian Forests are randomized classification models that can be updated online. This paper identifies a statistical problem with keeping their lifetime parameter fixed: that choice hinders consistency. Consistency concerns whether learning can approach the appropriate statistical target as the amount of data increases, so the parameter choice affects more than immediate predictive performance.

The authors modify the algorithm to grow trees with lifetime parameters that increase with sample size. They also introduce an alternative updating rule that preserves the ability to operate online. The resulting procedure adjusts its tree construction as more observations arrive, and the analysis gives simple conditions under which consistency holds.

The theory further establishes a minimax-optimal rate for estimating a Lipschitz regression function, extending earlier results to arbitrary dimension. Minimax optimality describes the best achievable rate over the relevant function class. The result therefore combines a consistency guarantee with a sharper statement about how quickly estimation improves under that smoothness assumption, while retaining an online implementation.
neurips-2017-universal-consistency-and-m.tldr: A modified online Mondrian Forest achieves consistency under stated conditions and minimax-optimal rates for Lipschitz regression in arbitrary dimension.

paragraphs: Gaussian process inference becomes difficult at large scale because time and memory demands grow faster than dataset size. Sparse variational methods help, but standard sparsification can restrict the complexity of functions they approximate. This paper seeks a more expressive approximation without imposing the same computational burden on every part of the model.

The proposed model decouples the representations of the mean and covariance functions in a reproducing kernel Hilbert space. This new parameterization generalizes earlier models and supports stochastic gradient ascent. Its time and space complexity are linear in the number of mean-function parameters, regardless of the chosen kernels, likelihoods, and inducing points.

The linearity claim concerns the mean representation’s parameter count, making it possible to expand that representation more affordably. This is the route by which the authors argue for expressive Gaussian process models at larger scales. Regression experiments report substantial improvements over previous sparse variational inference procedures, supporting the usefulness of separating the mean and covariance representations.
neurips-2017-variational-inference-for-g.tldr: Decoupling Gaussian process mean and covariance representations enables inference that scales linearly with mean parameters and improves reported regression performance.
